stat_summary: A YouGov food study found that 82% of British men describe themselves as meat-eaters, compared with 69% of women. Six per cent of Britons overall are vegetarian, including 8% of women and 3% of men. A further 11% call themselves flexitarian, 3% pescatarian and 2% vegan.

male.headline: Leave the Sausage Alone: 82 Per Cent of British Men Eat Meat, and They're Tired of Apologising
male.standfirst: New survey figures confirm what every bloke already knows from the wrong end of a gastropub menu: most British men still eat meat, and they are getting precisely zero peace about it.
male.image_caption: Terry, 44, and a pie that asked no questions.
body_paragraphs: New survey figures have confirmed what every bloke already knows from the wrong end of a gastropub menu: most British men still eat meat. Fully 82 per cent describe themselves as meat-eaters, against 69 per cent of women, and they receive, in return, precisely zero peace in which to finish a sausage.
“I ordered a chicken pie in a gastropub,” said Terry, 44, from Grimsby. “The waiter looked at me as if I'd asked for a badger. Nobody offered me a complimentary roast potato by way of thanks.”

The same study finds that only 3 per cent of men are vegetarian, against 8 per cent of women, which campaigners have taken as evidence that a silent carnivorous majority is going uncatered for. They are already calling for a National Meat Appreciation Week, and for a designated “no questions asked” section of every pub menu for men who are, in their words, “just trying to have their dinner”.
Yet where is the outrage? Where is the documentary? Britain's unapologetic pie man chews on, alone, with only a jug of gravy for company.
male.pull_quote: The waiter looked at me as if I'd asked for a badger. Nobody offered me a complimentary roast potato by way of thanks.

female.headline: She's Not Being Difficult: Women Are More Than Twice as Likely to Be Vegetarian, and It's Not a Phase
female.standfirst: Official polling has finally put a number on the quiet dietary diplomacy still being done by British women, and it does not look anything like a fuss over a side salad.
body_paragraphs: Official polling has at last put a number on the quiet dietary diplomacy still being done by British women. Eight per cent of women are vegetarian, against just 3 per cent of men – more than twice as many – while 69 per cent of women eat meat, compared with 82 per cent of men.
“He acts as if a mushroom risotto is a hostage situation,” said Aisha, 36, from Leicester. “I've been vegetarian since 2018 and I'm still the one who has to ring the restaurant ahead.”

Researchers note that younger women are far more likely to have dropped meat: among 16-to-24s, 19 per cent of women are vegetarian, against 6 per cent of men the same age. Campaigners are demanding a Menu Equality Act and a national apology for the phrase “but you can just have the vegetables from the Sunday roast”.
Until then, the country's unofficial advance party will keep ringing ahead, one forgotten meat-free option at a time.
female.pull_quote: I've been vegetarian since 2018 and I'm still the one who has to ring the restaurant ahead.
